title: Two-Step Sign-In
about: Add a second lock, so a stolen password alone can't get in.

cards.situation: A scammer far away got Mia's email password from a leak.

image.alt: Mia sits on her couch with her phone in her hoodie pocket. Far away, across a dotted line over the sea, a grey hooded scammer sits at a laptop with a sticky note on it: Mia's email password.

cards.prompt: Sign in to Mia's email, the way she does. **Tap each part.**

parts.job: Step 1: Mia types her password, then taps Next.
Step 2: a code arrives on Mia's phone: 481 902.
Mia types the code from her phone here, and her inbox opens: "Welcome back, Mia".

cards.explanation: Her password, then the code from her phone: that's how Mia gets in.

cards.prompt: The scammer types Mia's password and taps Next. **What happens?**

image.alt: The scammer at their laptop on Mia's email sign-in page. Step 1, Password, is filled in and the pointer is on Next. Far away, Mia has her phone in her pocket.
image.revealAlt: The scammer's screen now says Step 2, Enter the code, with an empty box. Far away, Mia's phone buzzes with the code 481 902. The scammer is stuck, with a question mark over their head.

options.text: The code goes to the scammer

cards.explanation: The code goes to Mia's phone, so the scammer is stuck at step 2.

cards.title: Two-step sign-in
cards.body:
This is **two-step sign-in**: your password, then a second lock, a **code** sent to your phone.

A scammer far away can steal a password, but not the phone in your pocket.

image.alt: The same picture, labelled. Step 1, the password: the scammer has it on a sticky note, with a green tick. Step 2, the code: it goes to the phone in Mia's pocket, and a red cross by the scammer shows they don't have it.

cards.prompt: A sign-in code arrives. Mia didn't sign in. **Tap what it means.**

image.alt: Mia on her couch watching TV at night. Her phone buzzes, and its lock screen shows 9:14 pm and a notification from Email: Your sign-in code is 481 902.
image.revealAlt: A bubble shows the scammer far away, stuck on Enter the code. Mia's phone now shows: Email, password changed, with a green tick.

options.nudge: When does a code get sent? Think back to the scammer's screen.

options.text: The app is testing my phone
options.nudge: When does a code get sent? Think back to the scammer's screen.

cards.explanation: Yes: a code only comes when someone types your password, so change it now.
cards.showAnswer: Someone has her password: codes only come when it's typed, so she changes it now.

cards.prompt: Mia gets a sign-in code. Then Leo messages her. **Tap what she should do.**

image.alt: Mia's phone. At the top, a notification: Your sign-in code is 481 902. Below, a message from Leo, shown as a circle with the letter L: Oops, I sent my code to you by mistake! Can you send it back?
image.revealAlt: The L circle has flipped over: behind it is the grey hooded scammer, typing at a laptop. The padlock by Mia's sign-in code is green and stays shut.

options.text: Send it back to help Leo
options.nudge: Look at the top of the screen: whose account is that code for?

options.text: Don't send it; change my password
Ask Leo why, then send it
options.nudge: Look at the top of the screen: whose account is that code for?

cards.explanation: Right: that code unlocks Mia's account, so it never goes to anyone, even a friend.
cards.showAnswer: Don't send it: the code unlocks Mia's account, and "Leo" could be a scammer using his account.

cards.prompt: Your phone has these apps. Which gets two-step sign-in first? **Tap the app to protect first.**

image.alt: Your phone's home screen with four apps: Game Club, Email, Music and Photos. Each has a small open padlock.
image.revealAlt: Email's padlock is shut, with a tag: Two-step on. Dotted lines run from Email to Game Club, Music and Photos, labelled can reset.

options.nudge: Think back to "Forgot password?": where do reset links go?

Think back to "Forgot password?": where do reset links go?

cards.explanation: Yes: your email can reset your other passwords, so lock it first.
cards.showAnswer: Email: whoever gets into it can reset the rest, so it gets two-step sign-in first.

cards.title: Recap
cards.body:
**Two-step sign-in** means a stolen password isn't enough, as long as you never share your code.

**Try this:** With a trusted adult, or on your own if you're 18+, turn on two-step sign-in for your email.

**Next:** Which second lock is hardest to break, and why your face beats a text.
